newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Matches to be played in the Spanish league championship this weekend: (league positions in parentheses; all kick-off times gmt)
With only one victory at home Sporting bring back veteran striker Julio Salinas to face an Atletico side without Jose Luis Caminero that is smarting from three successive defeats.
Barcelona's Bobby Robson has dropped striker Juan Pizzi for this top of the table clash against a Valencia side looking for their fourth successive win.
Real may be without defensive giant Fernando Hierro, who was injured in training on Thursday, in a crunch match against their 'bete noire' of recent years, Tenerife.
Led by Alfonso Perez and George Finidi, Betis will hope to keep up the pressure on the leaders against Espanyol, where there is dressing-room tension after a run of bad results.
Racing will be looking for three points at Hercules, who haven't won since the first game of the season and look strong candidates to go straight back to the second division.
Celta will be without influential midfielder Angel Merino against Victor Fernandez's Zaragoza, a side that urgently needs the points but tends to leave its bad luck at home.
Rayo were boosted by the midweek victory at Atletico Madrid, and will again look for leadership to striker Guilherme against Oviedo, who welcome back Russian midfielder Petr Dubovsky.
Athletic's Julen Guerrero has recovered his scoring touch and will be the main threat to Logrones, where coach Miguel Lotina is under pressure after three defeats in a row.
Extremadura have acquired a new lease of life since winning their first points at the top level last weekend, and will hope to score more against fellow relegation contenders, Compostela.
John Toshack's side have paid dividends on their summer spending spree, but striker Mickael Madar is out for a game in which Gheorghe Craioveanu will be the danger man for Real.
After narrowly escaping relegation, Valladolid have surprised everybody by moving up to fifth this season, while Sevilla -- once tipped as title contenders -- are struggling.
